qualification_observations: Fifty-three new actual-session/CSRF approval cases cover actor/payload/context binding, expiry, cancellation, replay, concurrent retries, database-write failure, unknown dispatch and ordinal-cache failures. Existing native handlers retain their behavior behind explicit review.

Uploaded metadata integration now prepares and approves before dispatch, and verifies the persisted description. Test-only telemetry adapters isolate span/source wiring; production execution always uses the server boundary.

Automatic code repair execution is removed. Dataset changes, edits and late responses invalidate frontend reviews. Receipts and job-request messages distinguish a native dispatch from downstream execution.

Initial full regression retained one legacy integration assertion expecting execution without the newly required approval. Corrected integration verifies the approved flow and persisted data; the entire unchanged marked suite passed.

Two browser diagnostics retained incorrect selectors (badge checkmark and relative receipt scope). The real mutation/expanded receipt were visible in both; corrected selectors assert keyboard dispatch, opened details and persisted description. No requirement, timeout, dataset, rounds, skip or coverage gate was weakened.

Six full-suite skips require a live model engine, local .env or four optional installed SDK checks. Screenshots of the actual review and receipt were visually inspected. Disposable credentials are absent from retained logs.

Final UI regression covers cancellation uncertainty, superseded preparation and changing away from and back to a dataset. Initial failures identified missing ngOnInit in two test fixtures; final tests install actual dataset subscriptions and all 550 pass.
limits: One native typed dispatch only: most actions hand settings to the frontend. Its receipt does not grant or prove a downstream job, immutable execution, independent review, human organizational approval or customer acceptance.

REST users retain installation-wide dataset access; project developer/reviewer/admin authorization, customer egress/retention and policy packages remain open. Actor-bound approvals are not project isolation.

Recorded-context freshness is not a transaction/snapshot across mutable form state, concurrent pipeline writers, filesystem, Redis and database. Full input/partition/environment authority and resource budgets remain required.

Trusted controller/database/filesystem; SHA-256 envelopes are not independent signatures or protection against privileged local/database mutation. Database-result authenticity and distributed/restore guarantees are outside this packet.

Unknown dispatch blocks new preparation for that dataset. No automatic reconcile/reset/retry protocol exists. Completion/replay idempotence covers native dispatch only, not browser-event adoption or downstream publication.
Expert Python remains blocked; exact expert-code/input/environment approvals, gVisor isolation, transformations/scorers, replay and scoring are still mandatory unfinished D08 requirements.
Keyboard workflow uses a synthetic provider proposal and real backend; no live model-quality or comprehensive screen-reader/accessibility qualification is claimed.
Native Linux/production deployment, full recovery, independent clean reproduction, agentic D18-D26, technical release and customer/value gates remain open.
